question_text: A ramp rises from level ground at 60°, the angle being marked at the bottom vertex where the ramp starts. At one point on the ramp's surface four forces act together: an unknown force F directed up along the ramp (parallel to the slope), an unknown force R directed perpendicular to the ramp's surface, away from it, a known force of 6 N pulling horizontally to the left, and a known force of 10 N pulling straight downward. These four forces balance exactly. Work out the values of R and F.
figure_description: A ramp rises from a vertex at the lower left toward the upper right, making the marked angle of 60° with the horizontal ground. At one point on the ramp's surface four forces act: F points up the ramp, along the surface toward the upper right; R points perpendicular to the ramp's surface, away from it (up and to the left); a 3 N force points horizontally to the left; a 10 N force points vertically downward.

solution.approach: Resolve F, along the incline, and R, perpendicular to it, into horizontal and vertical parts, and balance them against the 3 N and 10 N forces.

steps.text: Write the directions of F and R measured from the horizontal ground; F runs along the incline and R stands perpendicular to it.
steps.equation: F at 60° above horizontal, R at 150° above horizontal

steps.text: Balance the horizontal forces at the point: the 3 N force pulls left, while F and R each contribute a horizontal part.
Balance the vertical forces at the point: the 10 N force pulls down, while F and R each contribute a vertical part.
Solve the two equations together for F and R.

common_mistakes.text: Matching F directly to the 3 N force and R directly to the 10 N force, without resolving their actual 60° and 150° directions, gives F = 3 N and R = 10 N.
